h1: AIRQ · Air Sensors Against the EPA's Own Targets
title: AIRQ | Air Sensors Against the EPA's Own Targets | Heuremen LLC
desc: AIRQ: how PurpleAir outdoor sensors within 200 metres of EPA regulatory monitors compare with the EPA's published performance targets for fine particulate sensors, 1 March to 30 June 2026, with 1 June to 29 September 2025 kept as the previous reading.
intro_html:
Do the sensors meet the targets the EPA wrote down?

The EPA published performance targets for PM2.5 air sensors in 2021: a slope of 1.0 plus or minus 0.35 against a reference monitor, an intercept within 5 micrograms per cubic metre, an R squared of at least 0.70, and an error of at most 7 micrograms (RMSE) or 30 percent (NRMSE). We take every public outdoor PurpleAir sensor within 200 metres of an EPA continuous monitor, compare the two on the same UTC days, and ask how many monitors have a sensor that meets all four targets. We score the raw map reading, the raw cf_1 reading, and the reading corrected for humidity by the published Barkjohn equation.
note_html: The targets are for testing, and nothing obliges a deployed sensor to meet them, so this is not a finding that any sensor fails a requirement. Each row is the share of monitors whose sensor does not meet the four targets, with a 95 percent interval over monitors (a monitor with several sensors counts once). One half is a single line, so a row reads ABOVE when the lower end is above one half, BELOW when the upper end is below one half, and otherwise cannot tell, with the reason beside it. Under 30 monitors a row reads cannot tell (TOO_WIDE_TO_RESOLVE). Sensor and monitor values are 24 hour means on UTC days, because the sensor service gives daily means on UTC days. Days where the two sensor channels disagree by 5 micrograms and 61 percent or more are left out, the cleaning rule of the same paper. Sensors near monitors may not be typical of sensors elsewhere. Plan, notes and code.
